MindWalk.why: bio-native AI drug-discovery company: it sells AI-integrated antibody discovery work to biopharma and is converting it into recurring LensAI SaaS and ReefIQ data-layer agreements, so its revenue rises as biopharma adopts AI drug discovery
MindWalk.evidence: MindWalk Q4 FY2026 call (07-22-2026): CEO - 'HYFT provides the biological representation. ReefIQ organizes a client's own data ... And LensAI is where the reasoning happens'; first two contracted recurring LensAI platform agreements signed in FY2026; FY2026 revenue C$15.6 million (+46%)

players.product: HYFT biological representation, ReefIQ data layer and LensAI platform for AI drug discovery

connects_to.relationship: antibody discovery and AI drug-discovery services (client named by the filer)

contracts.signal: Sanofi (Sanofi Pasteur) is named among MindWalk's clients on its Q4 FY2026 call: CEO Jennifer Bath said MindWalk's discovery work for clients has put more than 20 molecules into the clinic, and among the clients it can name are Johnson & Johnson's Janssen vaccines, Sanofi Pasteur, argenx, IDEXX Laboratories and Xencor.

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year ended April 30, 2026; Canadian dollars, preliminary pending the 20-F), CFO Scott Areglado: revenue grew 46% to C$15.6 million from C$10.6 million; Q4 revenue was C$4.1 million, up 50% from C$2.7 million. Gross margin expanded to C$9.1 million or 59% of revenue from C$5.7 million or 54% (Q4: C$2.5 million or 61% vs C$1.6 million or 58%), reflecting a mix shift toward platform and higher-margin service work plus efficiencies after the divestiture. Net loss from continuing operations was C$15.1 million vs C$33.1 million (C$0.33 vs C$0.99 per share); net loss was approximately C$14 million vs C$30.2 million; Q4 net loss from continuing operations was C$3.9 million vs C$3.4 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue C$15.6 million (+46%); Q4 revenue C$4.1 million (+50%); gross margin 59% (Q4 61%); net loss from continuing operations C$15.1 million

quarterly_data.signal: Costs, cash and outlook (CFO Scott Areglado): total operating expenses were C$24.1 million vs C$42.6 million, but the prior year included C$21.2 million and C$1.5 million of intangible-asset amortization and impairment that did not recur; on a comparable basis operating expenses rose about C$4.2 million on deliberate investment in commercial infrastructure. R&D was C$4.9 million vs C$4.2 million and sales and marketing C$5.9 million vs C$3.6 million (more staff and North American business development capacity); Q4 R&D C$1.6 million vs C$0.8 million, Q4 sales and marketing C$1.5 million vs C$0.9 million. Cash was C$11.5 million at April 30, 2026 vs C$10.8 million a year earlier. The CFO expects operating expenses to increase as MindWalk invests in its pipeline assets and ReefIQ, giving no specific percentage and saying the company is 'trying to run as tight a ship as we can'.
quarterly_data.figure: opex C$24.1 million (C$42.6 million); cash C$11.5 million; operating expenses expected to increase

quarterly_data.signal: First recurring platform revenue: MindWalk signed its first enterprise-layer SaaS agreement for LensAI in the second half of FY2026 and a second contract in Q4 - the first two contracted recurring platform agreements and the first recurring platform revenue in the company's history. CFO: revenue is still almost primarily fee-for-service work; the first agreement was a modest amount, not significant to FY2026 revenue, and individual amounts are not disclosed. CEO Jennifer Bath: not material to revenue but 'pretty decent' - invoiced and paid, then recognized in equal monthly amounts over the agreed term, after the client moved from fee-for-service work to a SaaS license. The CFO expects SaaS to be a high-margin business but cannot give a number until compute costs and usage patterns are known.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 contracted recurring LensAI platform agreements; not significant to FY2026 revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Commercial model (CEO Jennifer Bath): in FY2026 LensAI was integrated into every new client program and clients began paying to add LensAI applications; double-digit clients are now in the LensAI portal accessing their data directly, with dozens more programs moving into that usage. The piecemeal fee-for-service introduction model has ended - clients are now asked to contract in a partnership model or take a SaaS license. ReefIQ can be packaged on its own, works with any AI model, agentic AI or other platforms, and can be bought as orchestration in a secure environment. The enterprise business development team was deepened, with two more senior professionals added in Boston and San Francisco.
quarterly_data.figure: double-digit clients in the LensAI portal; dozens more programs moving into usage

quarterly_data.signal: Platform and next validation (CEO Jennifer Bath): HYFT provides the biological representation (20 years of curated, function-annotated biology), ReefIQ - launched this year - organizes a client's own discovery data into governed biological context, and LensAI is the reasoning layer (target discovery, candidate diligence, portfolio decision support, agentic AI workflows). She named the next rung to watch as clients engaging ReefIQ to organize and manage their data across their broader estate, targeting the same profile as the first SaaS client. On July 1, 2026 MindWalk filed a patent application extending its foundational HYFT patent to the architecture that organizes biological context.
quarterly_data.figure: ReefIQ launched; HYFT patent application filed July 1, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Track record (CEO Jennifer Bath): MindWalk's discovery work for clients has put more than 20 molecules into the clinic, counting only clients it is free to name (more including confidential programs); 10 are in active Phase I through Phase III trials and four are first-in-class, backed by more than 400 peer-reviewed publications and issued patents. Named clients include Johnson & Johnson's Janssen vaccines, Sanofi Pasteur, argenx, IDEXX Laboratories and Xencor. In June 2026 a client's therapeutic for a rare autoimmune disease was approved by the FDA and launched; MindWalk supplied the anti-idiotypic reagents the client used to build and validate its bioanalytical assays, including in response to a direct agency request.
quarterly_data.figure: 20+ client molecules in the clinic; 10 in Phase I-III; 4 first-in-class; 400+ publications and issued patents
quarterly_data.counterparty: Johnson & Johnson (Janssen vaccines), argenx, IDEXX Laboratories, Xencor

quarterly_data.signal: Internal pipeline (CEO Jennifer Bath): the platform is now applied to MindWalk's own programs - a conserved pan-serotype target identified computationally and validated in vivo across two independent campaigns; a GLP-1 receptor agonist sequence designed in silico that in vitro activated the GLP-1 receptor comparable or superior to semaglutide; an influenza functional invariant found across more than 2,000 strains; and a pandemic response platform deployed this year against Ebola and Hantavirus. The owned pipeline covers dengue, influenza, GLP-1 and the pandemic platform. No pipeline product is in clinical trials; dengue cross-reactivity is being analysed through a third-party partner with more results expected over the next couple of quarters. Some assets have prospective partners lined up, and securing ring-fenced non-dilutive funding for the assets was a major focus last quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: influenza invariant across 2,000+ strains; no pipeline products in clinical trials

quarterly_data.signal: AMD (CEO Jennifer Bath): MindWalk calls AMD an engineering partner whose teams work with MindWalk's to optimize the infrastructure its AI platform runs on; its libraries were migrated off a CUDA-locked stack onto AMD's open ROCm stack as a joint build now running in daily production. Citing AMD's published case study: on Instinct MI300X hardware MindWalk screened roughly 170,000 antibody pairs in about 4.5 hours versus 145 days previously, cost per million samples in literature mining fell about 39% and embedding throughput rose about 70%. MindWalk was presenting at AMD Advancing AI 2026 from the call date.
quarterly_data.figure: ~170,000 antibody pairs in ~4.5 hours (vs 145 days); ~39% lower cost per million samples; ~70% higher embedding throughput
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: AI compute platform (GPUs / ROCm stack); described by MindWalk as an engineering partner

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio: early in FY2026 MindWalk sold its Netherlands wet-lab operations to AVS Bio; the CFO said the divestiture of the European operations generated non-dilutive capital without sacrificing revenue growth, and the CEO said computation and the remaining wet lab now run as one integrated system. The company completed its transition from ImmunoPrecise Antibodies to MindWalk Holdings Corp. in September 2025 as one unified commercial platform.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: buyer of the Netherlands wet-lab operations
